summary: This sermon examines the household codes in Ephesians 5-6, arguing that Paul was not prescribing timeless family structures but subverting first-century cultural norms to demonstrate Spirit-filled, mutually submissive relationships. The most radical command is that believers submit to one another out of reverence for Christ, which challenged both ancient honor-shame culture and modern individualism.
key_points: Mutual submission (Eph 5:21) is the core command, challenging both ancient and modern cultural values
Paul flips secular household codes upside down by addressing subordinates first and insisting relationships are mutually beneficial
Paul elevates those without cultural power, redefining authority according to Christ's self-sacrificial example
The passage is ultimately about the church as the working model of new creation, not just nuclear families
The church transforms the world through counter-cultural community, not through political power
big_idea: The church transforms the world by forming Christ-like, counter-cultural communities characterized by mutual submission and sacrificial love, living with a foot in both the present world and God's coming kingdom.
title: EPHESIANS: Radical Submission
